choices.misconception: I paired the numbers from 50 - 49 down to 4 - 3 and forgot the last pair, 2 - 1.
I thought each of the 49 gaps between neighbouring numbers gave a difference of 1.
I thought each of the 50 numbers gave a difference of 1, so I counted numbers instead of pairs.
I added all the numbers from 1 to 50 and ignored the minus signs.

hints: Look at the first two numbers together.
Group the terms in pairs, each a number minus the one just below it. Every pair has the same value, so the answer is that value times the number of pairs.
Each pair such as 50 - 49 or 2 - 1 equals 1. The 50 numbers make 25 pairs.

solutions.reliable: Group as (50 - 49) + (48 - 47) + ... + (2 - 1). Each bracket equals 1. There are 50 numbers, so there are 25 brackets, and the total is 25. The transferable idea: when signs alternate, pair neighbouring terms so each pair has the same simple value, then count the pairs carefully.
solutions.elegant: Add the two kinds of number separately: the even numbers 2 to 50 add to 650 and the odd numbers 1 to 49 add to 625, so the value is 650 - 625 = 25.

whyOnTest: Long alternating sums are designed for regrouping, and the traps are counting numbers instead of pairs.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
